subject.title: fix(canvas): bound A2UI JSONL file reads

question: Should Canvas guarantee that locally accepted A2UI JSONL files fit the actual Gateway RPC frame, or should 25 MiB be retained only as a memory-safety read limit with post-connect transport failures accepted?
rationale: The intended user-facing compatibility contract determines whether the bound must include JSON-RPC encoding overhead and negotiated policy rather than merely cap local buffering.

options.title: Budget the serialized request
options.body: Keep the bounded reader but reject inputs that cannot fit the encoded Gateway request, with an end-to-end large-payload proof.

options.title: Use a conservative raw limit
options.body: Choose and document a source-file ceiling that leaves framing headroom, accepting reduced maximum payload capacity.

options.title: Keep a reader-only cap
options.body: Retain 25 MiB solely for memory safety and update the PR claim/tests so they do not imply Gateway delivery compatibility.

recommendation.title: Budget the serialized request
recommendation.body: Keep the bounded reader but reject inputs that cannot fit the encoded Gateway request, with an end-to-end large-payload proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice depends on the Gateway wire-policy contract exposed to Canvas callers.
